subject: Acme Corp - Buying process & stakeholder mapping / exceptions
messages:

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + procurement checklist from today's discovery

Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — appreciated the clear demo and how Redwood handles latency and cost controls. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks as we map the internal process: 

- Timeline: procurement has a formal review window starting the week of June 22; preferred go-live by August 1 if approvals are quick.
- Decision criteria: price per token, latency SLA, and data residency are the top three for our infra team.
- Stakeholders: I'm shepherding this on our side; Tom (cc'd) is the engineering lead who will validate security requirements; Procurement (TBD) wants to run the checklist attached.

Could you: (1) share a one-page stakeholder map / mutual action plan (who from Redwood will own which checkboxes), and (2) confirm whether Redwood can entertain a short-term SLA/data residency exception or contract addendum if we commit to a 12-month spend?

Attached: Acme_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (procurement template)

Thanks,
Elena

- We have options for SLA/data residency exceptions depending on deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated/private). From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: [Internal] ACME - buying-process exceptions we should prepare for

Team — forwarding Elena's checklist and Marissa's MAP. We should pre-clear two asks I expect procurement to push back on:

1) Discount: they want to know if we can do an up-front discount for a 12-month commitment. We should propose an approval band (e.g., up to 10% with AE approval; >10% requires manager signoff).
2) SLA / Data residency exception: they may request a contractual residency clause or stricter SLA for hosted offering. Aditya — can you confirm if a contractual DPA + SOC2 + a carveout in uptime SLA is sufficient, or do we need to put them on Redwood Private to satisfy residency?

I've attached a pricing model that maps ARR buckets to approved discount levels. If we can pre-approve 10% for ACME, it'll make the procurement conversation much faster.

Attachments: pricing_model_v2.pdf

Rafael

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Internal] ACME - buying-process exceptions we should prepare for

Rafael / Marissa — quick security/ops note after reviewing Acme's checklist and the MAP: 

- SOC 2 Type II: we can provide our SOC 2 report and a standard DPA; that should satisfy most procurement controls.
- Data residency: if Acme requires strict physical residency in a specific region, hosted will be tricky unless we provision a dedicated private deployment in that region. For a short-term exception, we can offer an addendum committing to certain controls (access restrictions, encryption at rest, contractual data handling clauses) but we should spell out residual risk.
- SLA: we can agree to an SLA carveout for any non-standard latency guarantees, but we need to limit liability and tie the exception to a revenue commitment / term.

Neha (cc) — can you weigh in on procurement/legal appetite for an exception (discount + SLA carveout) and draft conditional language? I recommend we limit discounts to 10% without VP approval and require a PO plus DPA signature before exceptions take effect.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Security & Reliability | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Internal] ACME - buying-process exceptions we should prepare for

Marissa / Rafael / Aditya — I've reviewed the proposed approach and the risks. I can approve a conditional exception with the following guardrails: 

- Discount: approve up to 10% for the first 12 months on the hosted plan for deals <$250k ARR; any greater discount requires Director-level signoff.
- SLA carveout: we can accept a limited SLA modification for latency guarantees, but require explicit liability caps and an exclusion list.
- Data residency: we will not promise physical-region residency on hosted unless Acme purchases Redwood Private or we provision a dedicated pool in their requested region. As a temporary measure, we can sign a DPA and provide controls and a timebox for migration to Private if needed.

Conditions before exceptions take effect: signed PO (value and term), signed DPA addendum, and an agreed mutual action plan signed by both parties. Neha will draft the language and circulate.

Attaching: approved_terms_draft.docx

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Elena / Tom — thanks for the patience while we checked internally. Quick summary of what we can commit to and next steps: 

- Discount: Redwood can offer a 10% one-year discount on the hosted plan for a 12-month committed term (conditions apply).
- SLA / Latency: we can agree to a limited SLA carveout for specific latency windows with explicit liability caps; full latency guarantees requiring infrastructure changes will be scoped as part of a Private/dedicated deployment.
- Data residency: for strict physical residency, we recommend Redwood Private; alternatively we can sign a DPA and implement controls as a timeboxed mitigation while we evaluate Private.

Conditions (per Neha): exceptions take effect only after (1) signed PO, (2) signed DPA addendum, and (3) mutually signed MAP. Attaching draft of the next-steps M&A and the approved terms draft for your review.

Proposed next step: 30-min call on Wed 6/17 to review final terms and get procurement questions answered. Rafael will bring final pricing and the discount paperwork; Neha will be on standby for legal language.
